findings.evidence: Lines 108 and 165: `{H : Type*} [Monoid H] (f : H →* G)`; Mathlib's `Rep.shortExact_res` (Rep/Res.lean:122) is likewise stated under `[Monoid H]`.
findings.fix: Replace "group homomorphism" with "monoid homomorphism `H →* G`" in the module docstring.
findings.issue: Module docstring says the sequences "stay short exact after restriction along any group homomorphism", but `upSES_res_shortExact`/`downSES_res_shortExact` are stated for any monoid homomorphism `f : H →* G` with `[Monoid H]` (their own docstrings say "monoid homomorphism"). The overview understates the scope a reader can use.

findings.evidence: Lines 31-38 list only `up`/`upπ`/`upSES`, `down`/`downι`/`downSES` and the four `shortExact` lemmas; `upπIsCokernel` (line 74) and `downιIsKernel` (line 131) appear nowhere in the docstring.
findings.fix: Add `Rep.upπIsCokernel`, `Rep.downιIsKernel` to Main definitions and `Rep.upSES_def`, `Rep.downSES_def` to Main statements, with a sentence saying the definitions are opaque and consumers go through these universal properties.
findings.issue: `## Main definitions` omits `upπIsCokernel`/`downιIsKernel` and `## Main statements` omits `upSES_def`/`downSES_def`. With `up`/`down`/`upSES`/`downSES` bodies unexposed (no `@[expose]`, per the PR description), these are the only way to build maps out of `up A` / into `down A` and the only way to see what the sequence's maps are; the docstring as written tells a reader nothing about how to use the file.

summary: Docstrings are accurate on the mathematics, but the module docstring understates the restriction lemmas' generality and its Main definitions/statements index omits the only public handles on `up`/`down` (their universal properties and the `_def` characterisations), which matters because the bodies are unexposed.
